1. (Currently amended) A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising:
a ring oscillator entropy source configured to generate a plurality of independent first entropy values;
a permutation or hash function logic circuit configured to receive and apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to generate a second entropy value, wherein the permutation or hash function logic circuit is physically distinct from the ring oscillator entropy source;
a pseudorandom number generator logic circuit configured to be seeded with the second entropy value and to generate a random number; and
a cryptographic logic circuit configured to produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number, wherein the cryptographic logic circuit is physically distinct from the pseudorandom number generator logic circuit.

2. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the cryptographic logic circuit is configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

3. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the cryptographic logic circuit is configured to at least:
implement a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

4. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the ring oscillator entropy source comprises at least two independent ring oscillators, each configured to generate independent entropy values.

5. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the ring oscillator entropy source is a single ring oscillator configured to generate the plurality of independent first entropy values.

6. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the entropy source comprises a plurality of independent hardware entropy sources, each configured to generate independent entropy values that are combined to form the plurality of independent first entropy values.

7. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the permutation or hash function logic circuit is configured to apply the plurality of independent first entropy values to a permutation function.

8. (Currently amended) The system of claim 7, wherein the permutation or hash function logic circuit is configured to:
divide the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
apply the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenate the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

9. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the permutation or hash function logic circuit is configured to apply the plurality of independent first entropy values to a hash function.

10. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the permutation or hash function logic circuit is configured to apply the plurality of independent first entropy values to a bit-mixer.

11. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the permutation or hash function logic circuit is configured to selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

12. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the permutation or hash function logic circuit is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.

13. (Currently amended) A method of providing security in a computer system, comprising:
receiving a plurality of independent first entropy values from a ring oscillator entropy source;
applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a permutation function or hash function to generate a second entropy value;
seeding a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
generating a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
producing a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

15. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes at least:
implementing a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

16. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the ring oscillator entropy source comprises at least two independent ring oscillators, each configured to generate independent entropy values.

17. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the ring oscillator entropy source is a single ring oscillator configured to generate the plurality of independent first entropy values.

18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the entropy source comprises a plurality of independent hardware entropy sources, each configured to generate independent entropy values that are combined to form the plurality of independent first entropy values.

19. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a permutation function.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 19, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes:
dividing the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
applying the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenating the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

21. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a hash function.

22. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a bit-mixer.

23. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes selectively applying multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

24. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.
